points.headline: Voters turn on AI data centers, and the industry starts to adjust.
points.body: The US midterms went badly for data center projects and their backers, from Senate races to local rezoning votes, and Texas, the fastest-growing market, may lose its lead after the blue wave. Meta warned investors the backlash could slow AI expansion, OpenAI said it will stop using NDAs with public officials on data center deals, and protests demanding a building moratorium are planned across Europe.

points.headline: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber, a bug-hunting model trained to stay in scope.
points.body: GPT-6 Cyber finds exploitable vulnerabilities and drafts fixes, and OpenAI says it avoided attacking out-of-scope services more than 99 percent of the time. Coverage asks whether a model alone is enough while labs face growing scrutiny over how they protect digital infrastructure.

points.headline: Claude tools under security scrutiny.
points.body: Anthropic declined to fix a Claude Dispatch flaw that researchers say can be chained into remote command execution across corporate boundaries. A separate GitHub issue reporting that Claude Code sends the user's email address to websites became the top Hacker News thread of the day, with over 1,100 points.

points.headline: AI agents move into the workplace, and security follows the money.
points.body: Perplexity launched always-on "Teammates" agents for work, AWS refitted Kiro to orchestrate agents, and Airbnb plans an AI travel agent for early 2027. Cloudflare's CEO called agents a bane for some website operators, while Palo Alto Networks is reportedly in talks to buy agent security startup Clutch for $500M.

points.headline: Humanoids hit the stock market as robot foundation models multiply.
points.body: Agility Robotics became the first US legged humanoid maker on Nasdaq, closing day one only 2 percent up, which invited questions about the market. Meanwhile NVIDIA released Cosmos 3 open models for interactive world simulation and AGIBOT's GO-3 Preview topped three embodied AI benchmarks.

points.headline: Assistants get faces and voices: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash and Meta Muse.
points.body: Google released Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, a cheaper and faster multimodal model that handles longer clips. Meta gave its Muse agent a real-time voice mode and lets US users video chat with it as an animated avatar, ahead of a dedicated wearable.
